title: Failed or aborted movement is published as successfully settled
evidence: Failure exits route continuation but enters the common settlement path
The settlement path does not retain FPathFollowingResult/origin/bLeftAnchor and unconditionally emits MoveSettled for player orders
AI AP is spent after the same path regardless of move result
impact: False tutorial or quest progress, success audio on failure and wrong AP policy for no-leave/engine-stuck cases.
recommendation: Introduce a typed movement transaction and terminal result; keep pose settlement shared but gate AP, audio, tutorial and quest output by the actual result and whether the pawn left its anchor.
change_risk: High; the contract is shared by player movement, AI movement, cover hugging, tutorial and quest events.
verification: Truth-table tests for request rejection, abort before leave, stuck at anchor, interruption after leave, successful route/cover hug and pawn loss.

title: Tactical HUD leaks the count of hidden enemies
dependency_edges: EnemyCountText -> GetAliveEnemyCount -> TurnManager full enemy side
evidence: Blueprint node A62206904B9B469926B54983E1BF4B29 is connected from OnUnitsStateChanged to EnemyCountText
A visibility-gated GetVisibleEnemyCount API already exists next to the unsafe API
impact: The player learns unseen encounter size, violating the fog knowledge contract.
recommendation: Bind EnemyCountText to GetVisibleEnemyCount and add a Blueprint structural validator plus a hidden/visible enemy functional test.
verification: With one visible and one hidden living enemy the HUD shows one while combat outcome still uses the full alive count.

title: Enemy activation has no liveness token when the current unit disappears
dependency_edges: TurnManager current enemy -> AI completion callback
scenario deactivation -> controller tick disabled -> combat unregister
evidence: The enemy queue advances only from HandleEnemyUnitFinished
Unregister corrects the index only when removing an element before, not equal to, the current index
There is no TurnManager activation token or bounded watchdog
impact: If the current AI is removed without callback the enemy phase can stall; a late callback after removal can skip the next compacted element.
recommendation: Use a generation-bound, once-only activation token; current-unit unregister performs idempotent cancel-and-advance and stale callbacks are ignored.
change_risk: Medium-High; sequence semantics must stay strictly one enemy at a time.
verification: Functional fault injection that destroys, unregisters, unpossesses and scenario-deactivates the current enemy at several execution steps.

title: Mission readiness work is visible because there is no loading overlay
evidence: The project backlog explicitly records a visible multi-stage pause and missing overlay
Fog grid build/raster/upload is synchronous, although current logs place the fog portion near 85-95 ms rather than seconds
impact: The player sees an unfinished scene and can briefly see encounter staging before fog is authoritative.
recommendation: Show a full-screen overlay at scenario request and remove it only on readiness; profile before attempting incremental or asynchronous fog work.
verification: Instrument request-to-Scenario.Ready and verify the scene cannot be observed or controlled under the overlay on both scenarios.

title: The repository has no reproducible Game/Shipping cook and stage gate
dependency_edges: Quest primary asset -> AssetManager scan with CookRule Unknown
soft scenario assets -> unspecified cook inclusion
evidence: The project wrapper builds only XRU1Editor
No MapsToCook/BuildCookRun/package profile was found
.github/workflows contains no workflow
impact: An editor build does not establish that Game Development/Shipping compile, soft-referenced content cooks or the staged game runs.
recommendation: Add a local UE 5.7 validation wrapper for non-unity Editor/Game, tests, data validation, explicit-map cook/stage and smoke; promote it to a self-hosted Windows CI gate later.
verification: Preserve build receipts, cook manifest, automation report and clean-folder Development/Shipping smoke results.

title: Automation coverage stops at pure AI scoring
evidence: Only seven project tests exist and all exercise world-free ScorePositionFacts
All seven passed in the current editor run
No project functional tests cover stateful gameplay
impact: Lifecycle regressions in the most coupled flows are detected manually and late.
recommendation: Create XRU1.Smoke with map load, scenario/quest lifecycle, movement failure, enemy removal, fog knowledge, retry, corruption and staged-asset checks.
verification: Run headless on UE 5.7 and archive machine-readable Automation results.

title: Logical feature directories have bidirectional include dependencies
evidence: Direct include parsing found 608 edges, 170 cross-area edges and 27 directed area pairs
Six bidirectional area pairs exist inside the single XRU1 module
The actual UE module graph has no cycles
impact: Feature changes cross presentation/domain boundaries and broaden regression and rebuild surfaces.
recommendation: Define allowed logical edges and enforce them with an include-boundary check; remove reverse edges through narrow DTO/read-model/command seams as touched.
change_risk: Low for the guard, Medium for dependency cleanup.
verification: Boundary script fails only on newly forbidden edges and the count trends down without forcing a big-bang move.

title: Build declarations do not express the real runtime/editor contract
dependency_edges: runtime XRU1 -> conditional editor authoring dependencies
evidence: All runtime dependencies are Public and the Private list is empty
Broad PublicIncludePaths export every area
Direct dependencies are missing or misclassified in several modules
Reflected editor authoring libraries live in the runtime module
impact: Transitive compilation hides missing dependencies and physical separation has a large, fragile public surface.
recommendation: Declare direct dependencies with minimal visibility and add XRU1Editor using compatibility wrappers/CoreRedirects and asset validation rather than moving reflected classes blindly.
change_risk: Medium; script package changes can invalidate Blueprint/StateTree references.
verification: Non-unity Editor/Game builds, Blueprint parent scan, StateTree validation, cook and staged smoke.

title: Player and AI controllers are responsibility hotspots
evidence: TacticalPlayerController totals 4054 lines and about 97 definitions
UnitAIController totals 4557 lines and about 63 definitions
Each contains multiple independently changing responsibility clusters
impact: Changes have a wide regression surface and most behavior cannot be unit-tested without a world/controller instance.
recommendation: Keep both as facades and extract pure scorer, activation/route executor and player command/selection/preview/camera/tutorial collaborators incrementally under characterization tests.
verification: Behavior traces and smoke tests remain identical; AI tuning is frozen during decomposition.

title: Campaign persistence failures are silently discarded
dependency_edges: victory -> mutate save -> ignored SaveCampaign result
evidence: StartNewCampaign and victory flow ignore SaveGameToSlot failure
A corrupt/wrong-class existing slot enables Continue but failed load leaves the screen without feedback
impact: The latest progress can be lost or Continue can appear nonfunctional without a diagnosable reason.
recommendation: Return typed persistence results, log technical causes, show a user-facing recovery path and quarantine invalid slots.
verification: Tests for corrupt and wrong-class slots, inaccessible path, write failure, recovery and successful round trip.

title: Asset load policy mixes hot-path synchronous loads and startup hard references
evidence: Twenty-three LoadSynchronous call sites and no actual async stream request were found
The GameInstance startup hard closure is about 82.25 MiB on-disk proxy and the five tracks/stingers are about 75.17 MiB
No packaged cold-cache trace or RAM measurement exists
impact: Possible first-use hitches and unnecessary early residency; the runtime magnitude is unknown.
recommendation: Measure packaged LoadTime and memory first; if confirmed, define screen/scenario bundles and preload asynchronously behind the readiness overlay while retaining strong handles.
verification: Cold-cache Development/Shipping traces for menu, hub, scenario start, first tutorial voice and first ability targeting.

title: Scenario retry does not capture generation across latent work
dependency_edges: event callback -> read current GameInstance RunId at publish time
evidence: RestartActiveScenario is BlueprintCallable and has no terminal-state guard
Quest event helper stamps the current generation instead of a generation captured by the originating action
The normal result-screen route is terminal, so an actual stale callback was not observed
impact: A late callback from an old run could be attributed to the new run if restart is invoked mid-action through another call site.
recommendation: Capture FScenarioRunHandle in latent actions/events and reject stale handles; guard C++ retry to terminal or explicit-abort states.
verification: Fault tests restart during move, aim, reaction, shot before/after FireCommit and delayed voice/tutorial callbacks.

title: Shared editor configuration auto-approves local code execution
dependency_edges: loopback HTTP tool request -> script executor -> editor Python console
evidence: bAutoApproveScripts=True is tracked in shared project config
The permission dialog is bypassed and execute_script can run Python
No request authentication is visible in the route handler
The module is Editor-only and engine default bind is loopback
impact: A local untrusted process can potentially use a developer workstation code-execution surface; packaged players are not exposed.
recommendation: Track a safe default, enable trust per user/session and add a random session token or explicit server-enable window.
verification: Unauthorized local request is rejected, authorized session works and packaged module lists contain no UnrealClaude.

title: Documentation and implementation disagree on current project contracts
evidence: AGENTS points to four deleted/renamed docs and absent template directories
GDD names a nonexistent cover function, stale fog profile and not-yet-created result widget
Code/config comments refer to absent docs 09/10/13/14
impact: Human and agent changes can start from incorrect constraints and repeat already completed work.
recommendation: After correctness changes, update GDD/architecture/backlog/AGENTS together and mark historical briefs superseded.
verification: All explicit markdown references resolve and sampled claims match source, config and Asset Registry.

title: Combat authority directly creates concrete UI screens
dependency_edges: Tactics GameMode -> UI manager -> concrete HUD/result widget
evidence: GameMode includes concrete widget headers and pushes screens
The root layout is initialized by PlayerController BeginPlay and guarded with null checks
impact: Presentation order and combat authority are coupled, but the current single-player prototype remains functional.
recommendation: After higher priorities, publish typed combat-start/result DTOs and let the presentation owner push screens; do not add a generic mediator framework.
verification: HUD/result behavior and retry/hub routes remain identical with GameMode free of concrete widget includes.

title: Attack and Overwatch duplicate large latent presentation graphs
evidence: Attack has 115 nodes and 8 variables
Overwatch has 107 nodes and 8 variables
The latent presentation topology is substantially similar while mechanical commit remains native
impact: Presentation fixes can diverge between normal and reaction shots.
recommendation: After action tests, extract a shared native/presentation helper while keeping FireCommit, AP, hit and damage in C++.
verification: Blueprint graph comparison and shot/reaction montage-notify/watchdog functional tests.

title: Runtime bindings are not torn down symmetrically
evidence: The mapping context is added but EndPlay does not remove it
Some selected-unit/tutorial subscriptions lack an explicit matching removal
AI has normal finish cleanup but no EndPlay override
impact: Nonstandard repeated possess/travel can create duplicate input or callbacks; normal world destruction limits the current risk.
recommendation: Create idempotent teardown and call it from EndPlay/UnPossess/reinitialization paths.
verification: Repeated travel and possess tests produce exactly one input action and one state callback.

title: Campaign save data has no explicit format version
evidence: No SaveFormatVersion or custom version is present
Legacy settings fields are intentionally retained, showing compatibility is already a concern
UE tagged-property serialization reduces risk for simple additive fields
impact: Future incompatible enum, roster or nested-structure changes will lack an explicit migration decision point.
recommendation: Add a version and migration switch immediately before the first incompatible schema change, with old-slot fixtures; do not build a large migration framework now.
verification: Load fixtures from at least two prior versions and validate invariants after migration.
